title: Upstream-live parity job: close the #222 disease the current gate leaves open
idea: check_issue_contract_parity.py only recomputes the SHA256 of the vendored bytes and compares it to a pinned SHA vendored alongside them, so it catches hand-edits to the vendored copy but is structurally blind to the source moving ahead - its own docstring says 'a match means the vendored bytes equal what the source generator LAST produced and pinned.' That is exactly the #222 stale-mirror failure (343 cards passed a mirror while the live contract had changed): if infiquetra-sdlc's gen_issue_contract.py evolves and nobody re-vendors, the gate stays green forever. Add a scheduled (nightly / weekly) CI job that checks out infiquetra-sdlc at HEAD, runs the generator, and diffs its output against the vendored artifacts, opening or updating a 'contract drift' issue on mismatch. This is opt-in and cannot block PRs (no sdlc checkout in the fast path), preserving the KTD3 hermetic design while finally detecting the drift direction that matters.
basis: plugins/mission-control/config/generated/check_issue_contract_parity.py:15-21 docstring: 'Design (deliberately does NOT run the sdlc generator)... A match means the vendored bytes equal what the source generator last produced and pinned' - upstream advance is undetectable. Origin pain: grounding brief section 3, card_validator.py 343 cards / #222 stale hand-mirror.
outcome_shape: PR adding .github/workflows/contract-upstream-drift.yml (schedule: cron) plus a check_upstream_parity.py that clones infiquetra-sdlc, runs gen_issue_contract.py, and diffs; verified by a red run against a deliberately-reverted vendored artifact opening a labeled drift issue, and a green run when in sync.
dod_sketch: Merged .github/workflows/contract-upstream-drift.yml (cron) + check_upstream_parity.py; verified by a red run against a reverted vendored artifact opening a labeled drift issue and a green run in sync.

title: Bring sdlc-schema.json under the parity umbrella it is currently exempt from
idea: config/sdlc-schema.json is vendored from infiquetra-sdlc (the docstrings and migration_notes say so) yet, unlike the two issue-contract modules, it carries NO .sha256 sidecar and is absent from VENDORED_ARTIFACTS, so a hand-edit or a silent stale copy of the canonical board/routing/schema contract flips nothing red. This is the single largest un-guarded contract in the plugin: teams, boards, phase_board_map, wip_limits, review models all resolve from it. Emit a pinned sdlc-schema.json.sha256 at vendor time and add the file to the VENDORED_ARTIFACTS tuple so the existing gate and test_issue_contract_parity.py cover it with zero new machinery. The generalizable rule: every vendored contract artifact gets a sidecar the moment it lands, never bolted on per-incident.

Ship a machine-readable contract-consumers manifest (a consumers.json listing each contract artifact -> [repo, vendored-path, parity-gate-present?]) checked into infiquetra-sdlc as the source-side truth, plus a mission-control command that reads it to answer 'if I change this field, which repos re-vendor?' The manifest is the substrate idea T14-F1-1's cross-repo job iterates, and it makes the 4-repo contract-mirror pain from the grounding brief a queryable fact instead of tribal knowledge.

title: Declare pin-vs-float compat instead of the brittle exact-literal assertion
idea: sdlc-schema.json carries schema_version '2026-06-17' and migration_notes that carefully distinguish 'strictly additive' from breaking changes, but the ONLY consumer of that field pins it as a hardcoded exact string (test_prompt_alignment.py:121 asserts schema['schema_version'] == '2026-06-17'). So a legitimate additive bump - the very thing the migration_notes say is safe - breaks the test, while there is no logic that would reject an actually-incompatible schema. Replace the exact-literal pin with a declared compat contract: the schema gains a compat_floor / breaking-since field, and consumers assert 'vendored schema_version >= my required floor' rather than '== a frozen string.' This turns the migration_notes' additive-vs-breaking prose into enforced version-coupling semantics and stops additive bumps from tripping a false failure.

title: Cosmetic-vs-substantive drift classifier to kill false re-vendor churn
idea: The parity gate is pure SHA256 byte-identity, so a purely cosmetic upstream regeneration (a reordered comment, a reflowed docstring, a trailing-comma change) flips the hash and screams 'drifted - re-vendor' even when the actual DATA surface (the tuples and dicts the shim imports) is byte-for-byte semantically identical. That is friction: the operator burns a re-vendor cycle to chase a no-op change. Since issue_contract_shim.py and issue_contract_data.py are PURE DATA modules (REQUIRED_H3_HEADERS, SEMANTIC_CHECKS, EXECUTABLE_CHECKS, PLACEHOLDER_LINES), add a semantic-diff companion that, on a hash mismatch, imports both the vendored and the freshly-generated module and compares the exported __all__ objects, reporting 'cosmetic-only' vs 'semantic' drift. The SHA gate stays the hard invariant; the classifier just tells the human whether the re-vendor is load-bearing.
basis: check_issue_contract_parity.py:64 hashes raw bytes (hashlib.sha256(artifact.read_bytes())); issue_contract_shim.py:89-100 __all__ exports are pure tuples/dicts, making value-level comparison feasible - so byte drift and semantic drift are conflated today.
outcome_shape: PR adding a classify_drift() helper + CLI flag to the parity tooling that reports cosmetic-vs-semantic on mismatch, plus a unit test with a comment-only-changed fixture asserting 'cosmetic'; verified by the test distinguishing a whitespace change from a header-set change.
dod_sketch: Merged classify_drift() + CLI flag + unit test; verified a comment-only fixture reports 'cosmetic' and a header-set change reports 'semantic'.

title: Executable retired-vocabulary invariant: make the migration_note a test

Nothing asserts that phase_board_map, active board keys, cross_team_transfer targets, and wip_limits contain zero references to any status=retired_historical team or any retired_patterns entry. Add a guard test that derives the retired-vocabulary set from the schema itself (teams with retired status + retired_patterns) and asserts every active routing surface excludes it. This converts every future retirement's core promise into an executable invariant, so an incomplete rename campaign fails CI instead of silently leaving a live edge pointed at a dead term.

title: Provenance sidecars: record which upstream commit produced each vendored artifact
idea: The .sha256 manifests contain only a bare 64-char digest - they pin what the vendored bytes are but record nothing about WHERE they came from, so the question 'is this vendored copy stale?' cannot even be posed without guessing which infiquetra-sdlc commit generated it. Emit a .provenance.json beside each vendored artifact capturing {source_repo, source_commit_sha, generator_path, generated_at} at vendor time, and have the parity gate print it on both pass and fail. This is the missing coupling metadata that makes T14-F1-1's upstream-live check cheap (compare recorded source_commit to sdlc HEAD before doing any expensive regen) and gives every drift report a precise 're-vendor from commit X' instruction instead of 'go figure out the source state.'

outcome_shape: PR adding .provenance.json sidecars for each vendored artifact + gate output that prints provenance, and updating the vendoring generator contract to emit them; verified by the parity gate printing the recorded source commit and a test asserting each vendored artifact has a well-formed provenance sidecar.
dod_sketch: Merged .provenance.json sidecars + gate prints provenance + generator emits them; verified gate prints recorded source commit and a test asserts well-formed sidecar per artifact.

title: Upstream-staleness guard: turn the half-parity gate into a whole gate
idea: check_issue_contract_parity.py only proves vendored bytes equal what the source generator LAST produced and pinned — it cannot see that upstream has moved on, which is exactly the staleness class that let 343 cards pass a stale hand-mirror. Invert the manual 'did we re-vendor recently?' question into an automated freshness gate: a CI job (scheduled + PR) that reads the current pinned SHA from infiquetra-sdlc over `gh api` and compares it to each vendored `.sha256` manifest, failing loud when the source repo's fingerprint has advanced past the vendored one. This removes the human re-vendor cadence entirely — the gate tells you the moment a consumed contract goes stale, instead of a lucky re-verification catching it months later. Pair it with an auto-opened 're-vendor' PR body listing the changed artifacts.

No sdlc checkout, no generator run -- just stdlib hashlib.' The gate structurally cannot detect upstream advance; grounding brief §3 records the 343-card stale-mirror (#222) as staleness-vs-live-contract, precisely this blind spot.

title: Close the unpinned-vendor hole: SHA-pin sdlc-schema.json itself

That leaves the single largest vendored contract able to drift silently under a hand-edit, the exact failure mode the parity gate was built to kill. Remove the gap by generating and committing sdlc-schema.json.sha256 and adding the file to check_issue_contract_parity.py's VENDORED_ARTIFACTS tuple, so a hand-edit to the schema flips its hash and fails the gate like the two modules already do.

title: One registry-driven vendored-artifact guard replacing bespoke per-contract checkers
idea: Today each vendored contract gets its own hand-written parity checker (check_issue_contract_parity.py is bespoke to two modules), so every new vendored artifact re-implements hashlib boilerplate and the next one is likely to ship unguarded — as sdlc-schema.json already did. Remove the per-artifact hand-authoring step: declare all vendored contracts once in a `vendored_manifest.json` ({consumer_path, upstream_repo, upstream_path, pinned_sha}) and drive a single generic check_vendored.py over it. Adding a new consumed contract becomes a one-line registry entry that is guarded by construction, and the fleet gains a single source of truth for 'what do we vendor and from where.' The best per-artifact guard is no per-artifact guard.

A declarative manifest makes 'guarded' the default state rather than an act of remembering to hand-write a checker.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/mission-control/config/vendored_manifest.json + generic check_vendored.py that supersedes check_issue_contract_parity.py's artifact list; verified by test asserting every *.sha256 on disk is referenced by exactly one manifest entry (no unguarded vendor, no orphan manifest row).

title: Collapse the four-format CHANGELOG heading parser to one canonical format
idea: test_release_triad.py must support FOUR distinct CHANGELOG version-heading formats (bracketed/bare crossed with hyphen/em-dash) because the fleet never standardized the vocabulary of a release heading. That per-plugin format freedom is silent drift: the parser is fragile and a fifth variant would slip a version past the triad guard undetected. Invert freedom into a single canonical form — pick one heading grammar, add a lint that rejects any NEW heading not matching it, and shrink the release_triad parser toward one branch as plugins migrate. The best release-heading parser is a single regex because there is only one legal heading shape.

Four accepted grammars for one concept is vocabulary drift the guard tolerates rather than prevents.

The best 'did we miss a reference?' review is the one a test performs for you.

title: Machine-checkable contract-coupling policy: what pins, what floats, stated once
idea: The fleet silently mixes three pinning strategies with no stated coupling policy: semver in plugin.json, a date-string schema_version ('2026-06-17') in sdlc-schema.json, and SHA256 manifests on vendored modules. Which contracts must pin, which may float, and how a bump in one couples to another is re-decided ad hoc every time — the operator carries the rules in their head. Remove the recurring judgment call: write the coupling policy as a DECISIONS.md entry and encode it as a contract_coupling.json manifest (each contract → pin-kind + coupling rule + revisit condition), then validate on-disk reality against it. The best per-bump coupling decision is one already written down and enforced.

title: Auto-generated reverse-dependency map: which repos consume which contracts
idea: When a contract changes, the operator hand-reasons the blast radius — the consumer side is per-repo ad hoc across ~19 consumer repos, so 'who breaks if I change this?' is answered by memory and grep. Invert the investigation into a generated artifact: a blast_radius.py that scans every workspace repo for vendored .sha256 manifests and upstream declarations, builds the reverse-dependency graph (contract → consuming repos), and emits a committed CONSUMERS.md plus a PR comment listing affected repos whenever a source contract's fingerprint moves. This is the reverse-dependents view that `cargo tree -i` / npm dependents give for packages, applied to hand-vendored contracts. The best 'who consumes this?' step is a map that is always current because a job regenerates it.

Applied here to the vendored-contract seam the parity gate already treats as a producer/consumer pipeline (check_issue_contract_parity.py docstring frames mission-control as 'a CONSUMER of the issue-contract pipeline whose source of truth is infiquetra-sdlc').

title: Upstream-currency job: the parity gate proves frozen-copy stasis, not upstream truth
idea: check_issue_contract_parity.py deliberately never contacts infiquetra-sdlc; it recomputes each vendored artifact's SHA256 and compares to a .sha256 sidecar that is ITSELF vendored. So the gate is green whenever the copy matches its own frozen pin — even after upstream has advanced. This is the validate_card_body disease one level up: the pin is a hand-mirror of a moment in time. The fix is not to weaken the hermetic blocking gate but to add a SEPARATE scheduled, non-blocking CI job that fetches infiquetra-sdlc HEAD's generated artifact, recomputes its SHA, and opens or updates a tracking issue when the live upstream hash differs from the vendored pin. Blocking parity stays hermetic; currency becomes observable instead of silently stale.

Nothing in the gate detects upstream advancing past the pinned hash — a stale-but-green window is structurally invisible.
outcome_shape: PR adding .github/workflows/contract-currency.yml (scheduled) + plugins/mission-control/config/generated/check_upstream_currency.py that fetches the sdlc-published artifact hash and diffs against the vendored .sha256, emitting a gh issue payload on mismatch. Verified by a fixture test that feeds a divergent upstream hash and asserts a drift-issue body is produced (and a matching hash produces none).

title: Collapse the deliberate parallel houses: one ordered vocabulary source, not N mirrored tuples

The drift test degenerates into a one-line 'both import the same symbol' assertion. Crucially this must preserve {#tier-vocab-ordering}: the source stays ORDERED arrays (strongest-first MODELS, weakest-first EFFORTS) so index-based upgrade-only merges keep working — the manifest declares ladders, not sets.

title: Guard the guard: auto-discover every vendored artifact instead of trusting humans to register it
idea: The parity gate's coverage is a hand-maintained tuple — its own docstring says 'Adding a future vendored artifact here extends the gate with no other change,' i.e. it relies on a human remembering to append. So a newly vendored copy with no .sha256 sidecar is invisible to the drift guard: the drift-guard itself can drift. F3 reframes one level up — coverage should be discovered by convention, not enumerated by hand. Add a meta-guard that scans every plugins/*/config/generated/** file and every file bearing a SOURCE-OF-TRUTH provenance header, and asserts each has both a pinned sidecar and membership in the parity manifest. A vendored contract added without a pin fails CI immediately rather than riding along unguarded.

Verified: a fixture generated file dropped in without a sidecar makes the test fail with the offending path named.

title: Renames as an aliasable deprecation window, not a big-bang lockstep landing
idea: Cross-repo evidence shows renames executed as simultaneous lockstep landings (saga rename, Olympus->CAMPPS across 4 repos). F3 attacks the fixed assumption 'a rename is one synchronized edit event.' Reframe: a rename is a declarative ledger entry (old term, new term, alias-until date, forbid-after date). During the window both terms are accepted; a CI vocabulary lint only FAILS when a retired term reappears past its forbid-after date, and warns during the grace window. title: SHA pins conflate byte-identity with compatibility; separate them with explicit version bands
idea: The drift gate keys entirely on SHA256 byte-equality. F3 exposes the buried assumption: byte-identity is being used as the coupling primitive, but compatibility is a different relation. Byte-equality is a total order on bytes; compatibility is a partial order on semantics. So the gate cannot tell a whitespace/cosmetic upstream change from a required-field addition — it either cries wolf (blocks and forces a re-vendor on harmless drift) or, if relaxed, misses a breaking change that happens to look small. Reframe: each contract carries a declared semver + compatibility band, and the consumer declares 'I require issue-contract >= 2.1, < 3.' The currency check then classifies upstream movement as compatible-advance (auto-ok, informational) versus band-breaking (must act), instead of treating every byte as equally alarming.
basis: First principles: the parity gate compares hashlib.sha256 digests, a total order on bytes. Semantic compatibility is a partial order on meaning. A single-primitive gate keyed on bytes therefore cannot separate cosmetic drift from a required-field addition — the two produce indistinguishable hash flips — so it is forced to be either over-strict or unsafe. An explicit version band restores the missing semantic axis the hash cannot carry.
outcome_shape: PR replacing each .sha256 sidecar with a .contract.json (contract-version, compat-band, pinned SHA) and upgrading check_issue_contract_parity.py to enforce band membership alongside byte pinning. Verified by tests where an additive upstream minor bump passes the band check while a major bump fails it, with the SHA still pinned for exact-copy integrity.
kill_reason: Duplicate: semver version-band separating byte-identity from compatibility (auto-adopt additive vs gate breaking).

title: mRNA half-life: give every vendored contract mirror a self-expiring transcript
idea: In molecular biology's central dogma the genome (DNA) is never edited by the ribosome; the cell transcribes short-lived mRNA copies on demand, and each transcript carries a half-life so stale copies self-degrade rather than accumulate. Apply this to the fleet's hand-vendored contract mirrors (the class of failure behind `validate_card_body`, where 343 cards passed a stale hand-mirror while failing the live contract): every derived artifact under `plugins/mission-control/config/generated/` gets a header stamping (source-hash, derived-at, half-life-days) at generation time. A CI guard fails when any mirror outlives its half-life without a fresh re-derivation from `sdlc-schema.json`, forcing transcription rather than letting a copy silently ossify. This turns 'someone forgot to re-vendor' from an invisible latent bug into a scheduled, loud expiry.

The genome is the single source; transcripts are disposable and time-bounded. Directly analogous to fetch-don't-copy with enforced expiry on `config/generated/*.py`.

title: Structural expansion joints: declare which contract edges are welded and which are designed to move
idea: Civil engineers do not rigidly weld every joint in a bridge or rail line; uniform rigidity buckles under thermal expansion. They deliberately place expansion joints where movement is expected and rigid connections where load must not shift, and the drawings say which is which. The fleet has no declared coupling semantics: it is implicit and per-consumer whether a repo pins an exact contract version or floats on a compatible range, so CI cannot tell designed movement from dangerous drift. Introduce a `coupling-policy.yaml` at the contract-owner (mission-control) that declares, per consumer-contract edge, welded (exact pin, drift is a hard failure) vs expansion-joint (compatible-range, drift within range is expected and allowed). Drift guards then read the policy: buckling fails the build, designed movement passes quietly.
basis: Structural / civil engineering: expansion joints in bridges and continuous-welded rail deliberately allocate movement vs fixity (AASHTO bridge design practice; rail thermal-expansion joint design). The engineering insight is that uniform rigid coupling is a failure mode, not a virtue. Directly reframes version-coupling from 'pin everything' to a declared welded-vs-joint policy per edge.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/mission-control/config/coupling-policy.yaml` (schema + per-edge welded|expansion-joint declarations) and teaching the drift guard to consult it; verified by a test with one welded and one expansion-joint edge, asserting an in-range float on the joint passes while the same float on the welded edge fails.

title: Epidemiological contact tracing: rank exposed consumers by which fields they actually touch
idea: Public-health contact tracing does not treat all contacts equally; it computes an exposure graph and ranks contacts by proximity and duration so scarce attention goes to close contacts first, not everyone in the city. A contract change today has no blast-radius map across the ~19 independent consumer repos, so a schema diff is merged blind to who it exposes. Build a `blast_radius.py --diff <schema-change>` that treats the change as an infection origin, walks the consumer graph (repos + the specific fields each repo references, discovered by grep over consumer usage), and emits an exposure-ranked report: repos touching a changed field are close contacts, repos importing the schema but not the field are distant. The report attaches to the contract-change PR so reviewers see the true reach before merge, not after breakage.

The non-obvious import is exposure-weighting by which specific field a consumer touches, mirroring proximity-weighting of contacts, rather than a flat dependency list.

title: Aviation NOTAM broadcast: consumers subscribe to a contract, the owner broadcasts changes to them
idea: Aviation inverts the burden of staying current: pilots do not poll every airport for changes; the system maintains a subscription of relevant airspace and broadcasts a NOTAM (Notice to Airmen) to exactly the affected operators when something changes. The fleet's propagation is the opposite and broken: consumers hand-copy contracts and have no way to learn a source changed, so drift is discovered by accident (the `validate_card_body` class of latent staleness). Invert it: each consumer repo declares a `contracts.lock` manifest naming the contracts and versions it consumes; a fleet-level GitHub Action, triggered when a contract in mission-control changes, reads all registered `contracts.lock` files and opens a targeted NOTAM issue in each affected repo describing the change and the fields impacted. Propagation becomes push-based and addressed, not pull-based and forgotten.
basis: Aviation NOTAM (Notice to Air Missions) system (FAA/ICAO Annex 15): a push-based, subscription-scoped broadcast of changes to exactly the affected operators, replacing per-operator polling. The non-obvious move is inverting propagation direction (owner-broadcasts vs consumer-polls) via a `contracts.lock` subscription registry.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `contracts.lock` manifest schema, a repo-scanning registry builder, and a `.github/workflows/contract-notam.yml` that fans out targeted issues on contract change; verified end-to-end by editing a contract in a fixture and confirming a NOTAM issue is opened only in the repo whose `contracts.lock` names it.

title: RTS lockstep desync checksum: halt the fleet on first contract divergence, do not degrade
idea: Real-time-strategy multiplayer engines run lockstep simulations and exchange a per-frame checksum of world state; the instant any client's checksum diverges the session halts with a desync error rather than letting clients drift into silently different worlds, because a degraded shared reality is worse than a stop. Contract mirrors across the fleet have no such tripwire, so divergence (a re-vendored `sdlc-schema.json` in one place, a stale copy in another) accumulates unseen. Add a `contract_checksum_lockstep.py` fleet job that computes a normalized checksum of each consumer's effective contract and compares against the canonical source; on the first mismatch it HALTS by opening a single blocking issue naming the diverged repo, rather than auto-reconciling or warning-and-continuing. This deliberately mirrors the /outcome campaign's HALT-not-degrade decision, extending that same posture from run status to contract integrity.
basis: RTS lockstep networking desync detection: per-frame world-state checksums that halt on first divergence (well-documented in Age of Empires / StarCraft lockstep engineering writeups, e.g. Bettner & Terrano, 'GDC 2001: 1500 Archers on a 28.8'). The engineering principle is halt-on-desync over silent drift, which aligns with the fleet's binding {#outcome HALT-not-degrade} decision rather than contradicting it.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/mission-control/scripts/contract_checksum_lockstep.py` + a scheduled workflow that opens one blocking issue on first checksum mismatch; verified by injecting a one-field divergence into a fixture consumer and confirming the job halts and files exactly one issue naming that repo, and stays green when all checksums match.
dod_sketch: Merged contract_checksum_lockstep.py + scheduled workflow halting on first mismatch; verified a one-field divergence files exactly one issue naming the repo, all-match stays green.

title: Live-source liveness gate: fetch-don't-pin contract verification
idea: Flip the cache constraint to zero: instead of trusting the vendored SHA pin, fetch the CURRENT source contract at check time and diff against it. The existing parity gate only recomputes the SHA256 of vendored modules and compares to their pinned .sha256 sidecars — it proves the vendored bytes equal what was LAST pinned, never that they equal live source. A source that advanced without re-vendoring stays green, which is exactly the #222 failure mode (343 cards clean locally, failing the live contract). Add a scheduled workflow that git-fetches infiquetra-sdlc HEAD, re-runs gen_issue_contract.py, and diffs against the vendored artifacts, decoupled from the fast per-PR byte gate so the expensive checkout only runs nightly. The practical kernel even without full liveness is the diff-against-live signal that the pure byte gate structurally cannot produce.
basis: plugins/mission-control/config/generated/check_issue_contract_parity.py docstring: 'recomputes the SHA256 of each vendored module and compares it to its vendored .sha256 manifest. A match means the vendored bytes equal what the source generator last produced and pinned' — explicitly last-pinned, not live. Wired at .github/workflows/ci.yml:33-40. Grounding §3.1: re-vendored sdlc-schema.json after 343 cards failed live contract (#222).
outcome_shape: PR adding .github/workflows/contract-liveness.yml plus a fetch-and-diff script beside check_issue_contract_parity.py; verified by advancing the source generator without re-vendoring and observing the nightly job report drift that the existing SHA gate misses (green byte-gate + red liveness-gate on the same commit).
kill_reason: Duplicate: same fetch-live-source-and-diff nightly job decoupled from the byte gate.

title: One canonical ref, N zero hand-mirrors: contract resolved from a single pinned subtree
idea: Flip 'every consumer keeps its own copy' to 'nobody keeps a copy — all resolve one canonical artifact.' Today each repo hand-vendors sdlc-schema.json and the issue-contract modules, and each copy is an independent drift surface. Replace the N hand-mirrors with a single source ref (git subtree / submodule pin, or a single fetched URL resolved at CI time) that the parity gate dereferences, so there is exactly one place a version can be wrong. This respects the org's binding convention that contracts are schema-validated-in-CI with a self-describing index, NOT runtime-injected blobs (grounding §4) — the resolution happens at CI time against a pinned ref, never injected into an agent prompt at runtime. The kernel: collapse the drift surface from N copies to one pin, so a re-vendor is a single ref bump instead of a per-repo hand-copy.

title: Continuous cross-repo drift sweep: contract drift hunted, not stumbled upon
idea: Flip 'drift caught reactively on someone's PR or by lucky recall' to 'drift continuously hunted across the whole fleet.' A scheduled routine walks all consumer repos, diffs each vendored contract copy against source, and files a mission-control defect issue per drift with the offending file, pinned SHA, and live SHA. Today drift surfaces only when an operator remembers or gets lucky (stale-claim pattern, 2 repos) and contract copies silently diverge from source truth (2 repos). Extreme framing (check every hour, every repo) mines the kernel: a cron-scheduled sweep + a precise per-drift issue emitter so the fleet's contract health is a live dashboard, not tribal memory. Cheap-tier agents author the issues; nothing merges autonomously, only reversible issue creation.

The extreme (trust no cached vocabulary) yields the kernel: a single resolve-then-write guard that structurally cannot set a field that does not exist or act on a truncated page.

title: Manifest-driven autonomous rename campaign with all-green lockstep landing
idea: Flip 'one rename hand-copied across repos' to '100 renames, zero manual edits, landed atomically.' The saga rename and Olympus→CAMPPS were hand-copy lockstep churn across 4 repos — slow, error-prone, and leaving windows of a half-renamed fleet. Declare {old→new} tuples in one rename-manifest; a codemod engine applies them across every consumer repo, opens lockstep PRs, and a landing-coordinator merges in dependency order ONLY when all are simultaneously green, so the fleet is never partially renamed. Housed inside the existing saga or mission-control plugin (not a new plugin) to avoid consolidation burden. The kernel even if landing stays operator-gated: a dry-run codemod from a single manifest replaces the hand-copy dance and makes the blast radius explicit before a single PR opens.

title: Pin-vs-float compat manifest: auto-adopt additive contract changes, gate only breaking ones
idea: Flip both extremes — 'everything pinned' vs 'everything floats' — to mine the middle kernel. The SHA parity gate is binary: identical or drift. It cannot tell an additive, backward-compatible source change (a new optional field, safe to auto-adopt) from a breaking one (a removed/renamed required field, must gate). Byte-identity conflates 'changed' with 'incompatible,' forcing a manual re-vendor even for harmless additions and equally red-flagging both. Declare per-contract coupling semantics: a semver-style contract version plus a compat-mode (pinned = breaking-change gate; floating = auto-adopt additive) so CI auto-adopts additive diffs and halts only on breaking ones. The #222 incident was a genuine breaking divergence that SHOULD gate; the point is to stop treating every additive change with the same manual ceremony.
basis: First-principles: the parity gate recomputes and compares SHA256 (check_issue_contract_parity.py) — a pure byte comparison has no notion of backward compatibility, so an additive schema change (new optional enum value) and a breaking one (removed required field) both flip the hash identically and both demand a manual re-vendor. A declared contract-version + compat-mode is the minimum structure that lets CI distinguish safe-to-float from must-gate, eliminating manual ceremony for the safe majority while preserving the #222 gate for the breaking minority.
outcome_shape: PR adding a contract-version field + compat-policy manifest to plugins/mission-control/config/sdlc-schema.json and teaching the parity gate to auto-adopt additive diffs vs gate breaking ones; verified by two fixtures — an additive change that passes without re-vendor and a field-removal that fails the gate.
dod_sketch: Merged contract-version + compat-policy in sdlc-schema.json + parity gate auto-adopt-additive vs gate-breaking; verified an additive fixture passes without re-vendor and a field-removal fixture fails.

title: Self-registering consumer graph: instant who-consumes-X blast radius
idea: Flip 'zero knowledge of who consumes a contract' to 'every consumer known, 100% mapped.' Today discovering which repos vendor a given contract requires scanning 19 repos by hand (how the grounding pass itself found the drift). Make each vendoring gate self-register its copy — (repo, contract name, path, pinned SHA) — into one central consumers.json in infiquetra-sdlc (or context-library), so a source change instantly enumerates its exact blast radius and the drift sweep (T14-F6-3) fans out to precisely the affected repos instead of scanning the world. The kernel even at partial adoption: a queryable 'who consumes sdlc-schema' answer that replaces a full-fleet grep, turning contract-change planning from archaeology into a lookup.

No central registry of which repos consume which contract exists today.

title: Forbid contract mirrors: consumers exec the source-of-truth validator, and a lint bans hand-copies
idea: The 4-repo drift pain (343 'clean' cards failing the live contract because validate_card_body was a stale hand-copy of card_validator.py) is usually answered with sync automation or drift-guard CI — which keeps the copies and polices them forever. The uncomfortable structural fix is to abolish the copies: mission-control exposes card_validator.py (and the sdlc schema) as a stable, versioned CLI contract, consumer repos rewrite their checks to exec the installed plugin's validator at check time, and a lint in the context-library validate suite bans locally-implemented validation of contracts that have a canonical owner. Drift becomes impossible instead of detected, at the cost of a runtime dependency on plugin installation — a tradeoff worth surfacing explicitly.

title: Producer-push contract propagation: the source repo opens the refresh PRs, hand-copying abolished
idea: Invert the ownership of contract mirrors: today consumers hand-copy (validate_card_body, re-vendored sdlc-schema.json) and drift is discovered by incident. Instead, the source repo carries a consumer registry (repo, path, transform) beside each published contract, and a CI job on contract-change merge dispatches refresh PRs to every registered consumer; consumer CI independently fails if vendored bytes differ from registry-declared generated bytes. Drift becomes impossible to create silently in either direction — a human never hand-copies, and an unregistered copy is flagged by a workspace-wide sweep that greps for known contract fingerprints. This is structurally different from the obvious 'add drift-guard tests' because the guard lives with the producer, who is the only party that knows a change happened at time zero.

The 343-card incident shows consumer-side vigilance failed precisely because the consumer had no signal a change occurred; only the producer has that signal at the moment of change.
outcome_shape: Merged: `contracts/consumers.json` registry + a dispatch workflow in this repo (source of card_validator/sdlc vocab) that opens refresh PRs on contract change + one consumer repo converted to registry-declared generated vendoring as the reference implementation.

Every future vocabulary change (a new model, a new intent, a rename) becomes a one-file edit plus regen, and every new mirror is drift-proof by construction. Drift-guard tests themselves become auto-enumerated from the registry's declared producer/consumer pairs rather than hand-written per incident. Preserves {#tier-vocab-ordering}: the registry stores ordered ladders, and the renderer emits them in ladder order.

title: Consumer-driven contract tests (Pact-style) for vocabulary propagation
idea: Microservice teams stop schema drift with consumer-driven contract testing (Pact): each consumer publishes the contract it expects, and the provider's CI fails if it breaks any consumer's expectation. The fleet has the exact disease — validate_card_body was a stale hand-copy of card_validator.py, 343 'clean' cards failed the live contract. Ship a contract-broker convention: each contract copy (card validators, sdlc-schema, tier vocab) declares its source-of-truth provider; a CI guard fetches the provider and fails on byte/semantic drift, so a rename in the source breaks the consumer's build loudly instead of silently.

outcome_shape: Merged contract-manifest format + CI guard script that diffs each declared consumer copy against its provider and fails on drift, seeded with the card_validator/sdlc-schema pairs.

title: The marketplace is the contract bus: distribute shared contracts as plugin surface, making drift a version check
idea: Flip vendoring to its extreme opposite — no repo ever copies a contract; everything resolves from the source of truth at use time. Shared contracts (sdlc-schema.json, card_validator logic, tier vocabulary) ship inside the plugin that owns them (mission-control, saga) and consumer repos call the installed plugin's script instead of a hand-copied validate_card_body; the 343-cards-failed class of drift collapses into 'your installed plugin is version X, upstream is Y', which existing version-drift guards already know how to check. No new plugin (satisfying the groom-17-to-7 burden of proof) — this is a re-homing of contract copies into plugins that are already installed in the 8 repos where the ship-ceremony mining found saga/mission-control present.

Engages {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}: no new plugin is created; contract copies consolidate into existing installed plugins.
